questions.question: Visual search returns similar-looking but wrong items. What training rule fixes ranking order?
options: Bigger embedding dimensions blindly
More random training pairs
Trust in raw similarity scores
Same-item pairs closer than negatives by margin
questions.explanation: Ranking needs enforced separation. This lesson trains triplets with margins.

questions.question: What distance relationship defines a semi-hard negative in the helper?
options: d_an < d_ap
d_an > d_ap + margin
d_an = 0 for every class
d_ap < d_an < d_ap + margin
questions.explanation: The helper excludes negatives closer than the positive and those outside the margin, retaining negatives just beyond the positive distance.

questions.question: What does recall_at_k report for one query?
options: Whether at least one of the top-k gallery items has the query's label
The fraction of all gallery items returned
The mean Euclidean distance to every gallery vector
Whether the query was used during encoder training
questions.explanation: It takes top-k by dot-product similarity and uses any(...).mean() over the label matches.

questions.question: Why does Encoder.forward call F.normalize on its output?
options: It turns embeddings into one-hot class labels
It makes dot products behave as cosine similarities for retrieval
It doubles the embedding dimension
It sorts gallery images by filename
questions.explanation: Unit-normalized vectors make the dot product measure angular similarity, which is the score used by recall_at_k.

questions.question: What must be kept distinct when evaluating image retrieval?
options: The query labels versus the embedding dimension, because they must be equal
The gallery order versus the image colors, because colors are never used
Same-item retrieval versus same-class retrieval, because a class match is not always the identical item
Training accuracy versus pixel resolution, because they are the same metric
questions.explanation: A retrieval benchmark must define relevance precisely. Returning another image of the same class may be correct for class retrieval but wrong for exact-instance retrieval.

questions.question: If an anchor and positive are farther apart than a negative by more than the margin, what gradient pressure does triplet_loss apply?
options: It rewards the negative for being closer
It sets every embedding to zero immediately
It ignores the triplet because only labels matter
It pushes the anchor-positive distance down or the anchor-negative distance up until the margin is satisfied
questions.explanation: A positive hinge value causes gradients that reduce d_ap-d_an+margin, enforcing a margin between positive and negative distances.
